title: Unique lifting of factorizations across locally nilpotent ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq A$ a locally nilpotent ideal (every element of $J$ is nilpotent). For every monic polynomial $f\in A[T]$ and every factorization $\overline f=g_0h_0$ of its reduction $\overline f\in(A/J)[T]$ into monic polynomials $g_0,h_0\in(A/J)[T]$ generating the unit ideal of $(A/J)[T]$, there exist unique monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ and reductions $\overline g=g_0$, $\overline h=h_0$ modulo $J$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ALI (lemma-locally-nilpotent-henselian), essential surjectivity of etale algebras and the final factorization paragraph

proof.text: $J$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. Let $x\in J$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with $x\notin\mathfrak m$. Then $1=ax+m$ for some $a\in A$, $m\in\mathfrak m$. Since $ax\in J$ is nilpotent, say $(ax)^N=0$, the element $m=1-ax$ is a unit with inverse $1+ax+\dots+(ax)^{N-1}$, contradicting $m\in\mathfrak m$. Hence $x$ lies in every maximal ideal. (Stacks says 'It is clear that $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$'; Mathlib: mem_nilradical with nilradical_le_jacobson, Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Basic.lean:140.)

proof.text: $(A,J)$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $B$ be a finite $A$-algebra. The kernel of $B\to B/JB$ is the ideal $JB$, every element of which is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-nilpotent-extension] applied to $A\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent] applied to $(B,JB)$, every idempotent of $B/JB$ lifts to exactly one idempotent of $B$. This is the defining condition of a henselian pair. (Finiteness of $B$ is not even used.)

proof.text: Existence. By step 1, $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and by step 2 the pair $(A,J)$ is henselian; so the direction 'henselian $\Rightarrow$ factorizations lift' of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] applies to the given monic $f$ and the factorization $\overline f=g_0h_0$ into monic polynomials generating the unit ideal of $(A/J)[T]$: there are monic $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$, $\overline g=g_0$, $\overline h=h_0$. (Stacks deduces existence instead from the equivalence of etale algebras over $A$ and $A/J$ together with Lemma 0ALH; the route through 09XI (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1) and the idempotent definition of the DAG is used here because the DAG defines henselian pairs by idempotent lifting.)

proof.text: Coprimality lifts. Let $g,k\in A[T]$ with $g$ monic whose reductions $\overline g,\overline k$ generate the unit ideal of $(A/J)[T]$; then $g,k$ generate the unit ideal of $A[T]$. Put $M=A[T]/(g,k)$. It is a quotient of $A[T]/(g)$, which is a finite $A$-module because $g$ is monic [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]; so $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module. Since $A[T]/JA[T]=(A/J)[T]$, we get $M/JM=A[T]/(g,k,JA[T])=(A/J)[T]/(\overline g,\overline k)=0$, i.e. $JM=M$. As $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical (step 1), Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] gives $M=0$, i.e. $1=ug+vk$ for some $u,v\in A[T]$. (Only $J\subseteq\operatorname{rad}(A)$ is used here, not local nilpotence.)

source.place: written by an agent; Nakayama Lemma Tag 00DV (2), and the argument pattern of more-algebra.tex Lemma Tag 0ALJ/09XI (coprimality checked modulo an ideal in the radical); Stacks states no uniqueness lemma for lifted factorizations

proof.text: Uniqueness. Let $f=gh=g'h'$ with $g,h,g',h'\in A[T]$ monic, $\overline g=\overline{g'}=g_0$ and $\overline h=\overline{h'}=h_0$. If $A=0$ there is nothing to prove; otherwise $1\notin J$ (a nonzero ring has $1$ not nilpotent), so $A/J\neq0$ and reduction keeps the degree of a monic polynomial: $\deg g=\deg g_0=\deg g'$. By step 4 applied to the monic $g$ and $k=h'$ (whose reductions $g_0,h_0$ generate the unit ideal) there are $u,v$ with $ug+vh'=1$. Then $g'=ugg'+vh'g'=ugg'+vgh=g(ug'+vh)$, so $g'=gq$ with $q\in A[T]$. As $g$ is monic, $\deg(gq)=\deg g+\deg q$ and the leading coefficient of $gq$ is that of $q$; comparing with $g'$ monic of degree $\deg g$ gives $\deg q=0$ and $q=1$, i.e. $g'=g$. Then $g(h-h')=0$, and a monic polynomial is a nonzerodivisor in $A[T]$ (look at the leading coefficient of $g\cdot(h-h')$), so $h'=h$. (Mathlib pieces: IsCoprime.dvd_of_dvd_mul_left, Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_mul, Polynomial.eq_one_of_monic_natDegree_zero, Polynomial.Monic.mul_right_eq_zero_iff.)
